newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurd rebels try to throttle pro-Saddam city.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd rebels try to throttle pro-Saddam city.

text.p: Anti-Saddam Kurdish rebels on Wednesday attempted to tighten the noose around the key northern Iraqi city of Arbil and reverse losses in August to a rival faction backed by Baghdad, witnesses said.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) said 6,000 of its fighters were gathering at Barisan Valley 70 km (44 miles) northeast of Arbil near a strategic road into the city.
The group has wrested control of other main roads to Arbil, to the south and east, from the pro-Baghdad Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
"We have two roads going to Arbil and we are getting close to the third," senior PUK leader Kosrat Rassoul told Reuters.
He declined to say whether his forces would attack Arbil, a city of some 800,000 people, from their northern positions.
Rassoul once served as the head of a Kurdish regional administration in Arbil that crumbled amid inter-Kurdish feuds last year.
The KDP, of Massoud Barzani, captured the city six weeks ago with help from tank-led Iraqi troops in an assault that enraged Washington.
The United States fired missiles at military targets in southern Iraq in response to the fall of Arbil, which ruined U.S. aid, military and intelligence efforts in north Iraq.
Barzani's group has accused neighbouring Iran of sending men and munitions across the border to help Talabani as part of a regional rivalry between Tehran and Baghdad. Iran denies this.
Talabani says he will not storm Arbil, despite his military build-up.
"Iraqi forces are protecting Arbil. If we attack we will cause an alliance between KDP and Iraqi forces," Talabani told Turkish current affairs programme 32nd Day on Tuesday night.
He said he would be keeping an eye on talks between his rival group and U.S. officials in Washington set for Wednesday.
"The USA have cut in to the situation. We are waiting for the result of this (American initiative)," he said. A KDP delegation was to complain to U.S. officials about alleged Iranian intervention.
Washington, fearing any possible Iraqi or Iranian bid for influence in northern Iraq, has called for the factions to restart U.S.-brokered peace talks that faltered last year.
The United States leads a Western allied air force that shields the Kurds from any attack by Iraqi forces.
PUK fighters armed with assault rifles, heavy machineguns and rocket-propelled grenades set up positions in Barisan Valley, about 10 km (six miles) from the Shaqlawa road to Arbil.
"We have sent all the forces we could find to the Shaqlawa-Diyana area," local PUK commander Mustafa Saib Kadir said.
The group would have to fight its way through the KDP stronghold town of Salahuddin to reach Arbil from the northern road.
President Saddam Hussein sent an envoy to Tehran on Tuesday with a message for Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.

"The Iraqi envoy voiced Iraq's desire for good neighbourly relations with Iran and for expansion of mutual relations. He also called for cooperation and exchange of views between the two countries on regional issues," IRNA said. It did not name the envoy.
Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati was quoted on Wednesday as saying that Tehran was ready to mediate an end to the Kurdish fighting.
